answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Locking scores each identity by the divergence between its declared action distributions in consecutive epochs, weighted like settling strata: a stable agent compresses toward shale, dense and slow-changing. An identity whose behaviour shifts like a zephyr between epochs—fresh keypads mimicking established agents—fails the consistency threshold and its actions are discounted. Forgery requires sustaining a coherent behavioural trajectory across at least three epochs, each demanding genuine task execution and a crystal-clear audit trail of matched predictions.
